pr_title: i18n: Fix `get_tool_locale()` not return current locale at runtime
pr_body:
- Fixes: #100642 

According to documentation, `TranslationServer::get_tool_locale()` should return the same value as `get_locale()` at runtime, but now it returns fixed value `en` when no Translation loaded. This causes some issues about text shaping as https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/100642#issuecomment-2573389272 explained.

issue_context.title: [TextServer] Some texts are shaped accidently when use system font
issue_context.body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: v4.3.stable, v4.4.dev.mono.custom_build [89001f91d] 

### System information

Godot v4.4.dev.mono (89001f91d) - Windows 11 (build 22631) - System Locale: `zh_CN`

### Issue description

Input Chinese texts `工具系统，` and `经济系统，` and see shaped text in editor and runtime:

| Expected, Editor | Unexpected, Runtime |
|--------|--------|
| ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a7a2c5db-0e27-4de0-8637-c9be6b5f0cc3) | ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/75e46d37-f05b-48e2-abb4-fa1fa88bd5d2) |

1. When the characters `济` and `系` are combined, `系` is accidentally distorted.
2. It also affects the comma at the end (which should be at the bottom left).
3. It only happens at runtime and with fallback system fonts. Behaves normally in the editor or when specifying custom fonts.

### Steps to reproduce

N/A

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[TextShapeIssue.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18209174/TextShapeIssue.zip)

Note: This may not be consistent due to differences in system region or language.
comments: I do not see any difference between editor and runtime. Not sure if it's fully fixable, seems like two fonts are selected for different parts of text and neither have all required characters.

If set `Bidi > Language` to `zh_CN`, it also works as expected. So the issue may occur when falling back to default locale.

TextServer uses `get_tool_locale()` to get the current locale. According to documentation, it should return the same value as `get_locale()` at runtime, but I found that it returned fixed value `en`: 

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/1aaf20b1f1f3ab59f04db74b166540327a3f1f90/core/string/translation_server.cpp#L491-L510

This led to it using fonts in different languages to shape texts.

> TextServer uses get_tool_locale() to get the current locale. According to documentation, it should return the same value as get_locale() at runtime, but I found that it returned fixed value en:

This is expected behavior, it should only return system locale if you have translation files for this locale, no translations included, always assumed to be English.

> If set Bidi > Language to zh_CN, it also works as expected. So the issue may occur when falling back to default locale.

It's likely that incorrect language is causing wrong font selection order (can happen for both system and embedded fonts). And if you have `zh_CN` set as editor locale, it likely the reason it's looking different in the editor, editor locale is incorrectly applied to the opened project (should use translation context).

Hi!

I came here because I saw the PR. I have a couple questions:

1. Why are no translations loaded?
2. Is the game intended to be primarily written in Chinese for a chinese audience? (i.e. no english at all, or very little of it)
3. Is the game in English with english as main but will use chinese characters inside?

I'm trying to understand the context here.

Because it sounds the game is written mainly in chinese for a chinese audience, hence provides no translations, which causes Godot to assume english as fallback locale while trying to render chinese glyphs, and thus causing the shaping distortion.

We probably should have some way to force default single language without adding translations, since this is not an uncommon use case. But we definitely can't assume user system locale is supported by the project.

In cases where i18n is not required, we will develop projects directly in single language without using translations. In this case, it may not be appropriate for TextServer to get the current locale through translation context.

Let TextServer use `get_locale()` to get current locale would be easier to solve this as https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/101184#discussion_r1904370408 discussed.

> Let TextServer use get_locale() to get current locale would be easier to solve this as https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/101184#discussion_r1904370408 discussed.

The better way is probably to set language in the controls using `TranslationDomain` (which uses `get_locale`), and avoid direct calls to `get_tool_locale` at all. This will require a bit more changes but should have better editor/project locale separation. I'll look a doing it tomorrow.

@darksylinc This can happen in any project in non-English system and does not use translation.

I've found some previous issues that may be related: #93211, #91470

> The better way is probably to set language in the controls using TranslationDomain (which uses get_locale), and avoid direct calls to get_tool_locale at all.

Actually, this should be already implemented in #97918

review_comments: This is not how it supposed to work, if no translation is provided it should return `en`, since everything assumes default locale is English. Otherwise, any untranslated app will use whatever current user locale, which will result in multiple undesired effects (flipping UI if user locale is right-to-left for example).

If so, then I can only set the Bidi Language for each control when I don't have translation loaded? (even if I've already specified the language for the project)
Is it possible to let TextServer use `get_locale()` instead to get the current language?

> even if I've already specified the language for the project

Not sure if there's option to set language for the project (only `internationalization/locale/test`, which should probably be used instead of hardcoded `en` if set).
